headline: Bessent: 'In the spring, I asked our European allies to join us in putting secondary tariffs on China, on India.'
dek: Bessent: 'In the spring, I asked our European allies to join us in putting secondary tariffs on China, on India. They refused.
sources: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, interview on NBC's Meet the Press (Sunday Oct 18); Secretary of State Marco Rubio remarks Saturday Oct 17; carried by ET Now, Economic Times, LiveMint, HinduBusinessLine, eflip
fault_line: Who is really funding Russia's war machine: India and China buying discounted oil, or Europe — which backs Ukraine while buying $8B+ of Russian gas? And is Trump's 'pause' a masterstroke or a gift to Putin?

sections.what_happened: Bessent: 'In the spring, I asked our European allies to join us in putting secondary tariffs on China, on India. They refused. So why should the US bear the burden?' He said the Friday sanctions waiver under the Graham Act is a 60-day pause to assess impact, not lifted sanctions. Bessent accused Europe of 'financing the Russian war machine': 140 Yamal cargoes in H1 2026, 136 to Europe (Belgium, Spain, France, Netherlands), worth over $8B; US imports $4B Russian products ($1.8B fertilizer); Europe imports 'more than 10 times' that. Rubio (Sat): Graham Act waivers exist 'to study' pressures on global energy supplies from Iran war, Ansar Allah attacks on Saudi Arabia, Ukraine-Russia war.
sections.what_verified: Five outlets converge on identical quote text from the NBC interview; Rubio remarks independently corroborated; TOI adds Indian-American lawmaker pushback (Bera, Subramanyam criticising the waiver). The National corroborates Trump's Sunday defense of the waiver (Truth Social) and the St. Petersburg energy-ceasefire context. Executive-order mechanism (waiver 'in national interests') corroborated by prior scans.
sections.what_disputed: Yamal 136/140 cargo and $8B figures are Bessent's numbers — no independent verification yet; European rebuttal not yet in coverage. Framing 'pause not lift' is admin spin — executive order text leaves the waiver open-ended ('until such time as the President or Secretary of State determine further action appropriate'), which undercuts the clean '60-day' framing. Note timing: midterms <3 weeks out, cited by TradingView (0300-01) as affordability pressure.
sections.why_matters: The Western sanctions front fractures on camera: Washington's own Treasury chief accuses Europe of financing Russia while demanding Kyiv fight on — even as the US itself waives the sanctions law and buys Russian diesel. Lead with the hypocrisy split (playbook Tier-1 debate bait: US-Russia diesel deal), pocketbook frame (energy prices, midterms), quote Bessent precisely, label figures as his claims, note the open-ended EO text vs the '60-day' framing.
sections.context: Background: US/Russia sanctions — NEW (missed by prior scans): Bessent reveals US asked Europe to join secondary sanctions on China/India over Russian oil and was refused; Rubio/Bessent frame Friday waiver as 60-day pause; Bessent accuses Europe of financing Russia's war machine ($8B+ Yamal LNG, 136/140 cargoes to Europe)
